lines.text: Real programmers hate writing the same code twice. Today you’ll invent your own Scratch blocks!
Make a Block lets you give a name to a group of blocks.
Then one block does the whole job — your code gets shorter and easier to read.
An input (like size) is a value you give the block when you use it.
The same block can draw a small square or a big one.
The define hat says what the block does.
Using the block anywhere runs that code with the input you gave it.
If there’s a bug in your block, fix the define script once and every use is fixed.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
